2609.31569.title: Adapting for AI: How elementary teachers adjust their practices for an AI-integrated curriculum
2609.31569.paper_summary: Conversational AI tools are entering children's everyday experiences, and schools are interested in adopting them. However, successful classroom integration depends not only on the technology but also on the work teachers do to make it usable and appropriate for their students and classroom context. There is little known about how elementary teachers work as they implement conversational AI tools in real classrooms. In this study, we examine three teachers' experiences implementing an AI literacy and English Language Arts (ELA) curriculum built around ToyTalk, a conversational AI toy development platform, over 13 instructional days, a three-week summer camp. Drawing on daily individual reflections, group reflections, and post-camp interviews, we find that teachers' adaptive practices of repair, differentiation, translation, and balancing sit at the intersection of three tensions (technology, learner, and instruction). Teachers' understanding of AI and their role evolved over the camp experiences. From these findings, we contribute design implications and considerations for deploying conversational AI within elementary classrooms.
2609.31569.paper_summary_zh: 對話式人工智慧工具正進入兒童的日常生活，學校也對採用這些工具感興趣。<lb/>然而，成功的課堂整合不僅取決於技術，還取決於教師為使其適合學生和課堂環境所做的工作。<lb/>目前對於小學教師在實際課堂中實施對話式人工智慧工具的工作了解甚少。<lb/>在這項研究中，我們檢視三位教師在為期13天的教學日、三週的夏令營中實施圍繞ToyTalk（一個對話式人工智慧玩具開發平台）構建的人工智慧素養和英語語言藝術（ELA）課程的經驗。<lb/>根據每日的個人反思、小組反思和夏令營後的訪談，我們發現教師的修復、差異化、翻譯和平衡的適應性實踐位於三種緊張（技術、學習者和教學）的交匯處。<lb/>教師對人工智慧及其角色的理解在夏令營的經驗中不斷演變。<lb/>根據這些發現，我們提供了在小學課堂中部署對話式人工智慧的設計啟示和考量。
